Group allegedly stole millions in SNAP benefits, bought luxury cars: DA NEW YORK, N.Y. (PIX11) -- Eight people have been indicted for allegedly conspiring to steal millions of dollars from the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program over a two-year period.
 According to court statements and documents, between April 2023 and September 2025, Belal Hauter, 34, and a number of his associates allegedly used cloned EBT cards to steal more than $7 million in SNAP benefits.
 Image of Alleged EBT Fraud Operation Seized through Court-Authorized Warrant (Manhattan DA)
 Image of Alleged EBT Fraud Operation Seized through Court-Authorized Warrant (Manhattan DA)
 According to the investigation, the suspects first obtained point-of-sale (POS) systems and merchant processing accounts under the guise of a real or fictitious deli or grocery store. They then proceeded to use card skimmers to steal EBT account numbers and their associated PIN numbers. That information was then allegedly used to create cloned EBT cards, allowing the suspects access to any funds transferred to those compromised accounts.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Shortly after the money was loaded, the cards were then swiped, usually until the accounts were depleted. Court documents revealed that the stolen funds allegedly were sent to a number of international locations, as well as used to purchase multiple luxury vehicles.
  Get ongoing crime and safety coverage on our homepage  
 Along with Hauter, the alleged mastermind of the operation, his associates Abdulla Aezah, 35, Gregory Fabiani, 46, Milton Rios, 53, and Yvette Rivera, 58, face charges of conspiracy, grand larceny and identity theft. The alleged fraud impacted thousands of people, many of whom have not been reimbursed.
 "SNAP and EBT fraud harms New Yorkers in need of assistance and the New Yorkers whose tax dollars fund these essential programs," said District Attorney Bragg. "As alleged, this conspiracy created fraudulent merchant processing accounts for fraudulent delis and paid themselves by repeatedly swiping stolen EBT cards at point-of-sale systems associated with those accounts. The defendants allegedly tracked the timing of benefit funds and drained accounts before the legitimate SNAP recipient could buy food and other necessities, eventually stealing more than $7 million. I thank our law enforcement partners at DOI for their work in putting a stop to this fraud."
